structure.title: Covering Letter-Annual Report
structure.summary: This document is a regulatory filing by Tech Mahindra Limited dated June 23, 2025, addressed to BSE and NSE, regarding its 38th Annual General Meeting (AGM). It encloses the AGM Notice, Integrated Annual Report, and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2024-25, dispatched electronically to members. The AGM is scheduled for July 17, 2025, via video conference. The notice details ordinary business: adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY ended March 31, 2025, and confirmation of interim dividend (₹15/share) plus declaration of final dividend (₹30/share) for FY 2024-25. It also announces closure of the Register of Members and Share Transfer Books from July 5 to July 17, 2025, with a record date of July 4, 2025, for dividend payment.

nodes.title: 6. To consider and approve adoption and implementation of the Tech Mahindra Performance Share Plan 2025 of the Company (intro)

nodes.title: Approval for Tech Mahindra Performance Share Plan 2025
nodes.summary: The text outlines several resolutions for adopting the Tech Mahindra Performance Share Plan 2025 (TechM PSP 2025). The Board is authorized to implement the plan through the Tech Mahindra ESOP Trust, which will source shares via primary issue and transfer them to PSU grantees upon exercise, subject to payment and taxes; shares will rank pari-passu. Provisions address automatic adjustment of share numbers and prices for sub-division or consolidation, and potential increase in ceiling for corporate actions like rights or bonus issues per SEBI regulations. Members approve the Board to take all necessary actions, including listing and trading of shares, modifications to the plan, and settlement of related matters.

nodes.title: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT

structure.title: Tech Mahinndra - Annual Report 2024-25
structure.summary: Tech Mahindra's Integrated Annual Report FY2024-25 covers AI strategy 'AI Delivered Right' and case studies, including Garuda LLM and telecom automation. It details corporate overview, vision, values, global presence, and messages from leadership. The report includes strategy review, ESG roadmap, materiality assessment, enterprise risk management, and opportunities in cloud and AI. It provides extensive ESG disclosures on environment, social, and governance, including security governance, supply chain, health and safety, human rights, and BRSR Core assurance. Corporate governance report, shareholder information, financial statements (standalone and consolidated) with accounting policies and notes, subsidiary financials, glossary, and global office addresses are also included.

nodes.title: Tech Mahinndra - Annual Report 2024-25 (intro)
nodes.summary: The text discusses AI's ubiquity and the challenge of implementation, noting 74% of enterprises struggle to move from exploration to successful implementation. It introduces Tech Mahindra's 'AI Delivered Right' strategy to cut through hype and drive responsible, practical, scalable AI adoption. The strategy aims to equip clients with tools, frameworks, and processes to maximize ROI, modernize legacy systems, and focus on smart data practices, optimized spending, and ecosystem collaboration. Built on four pillars—Transformation, Productivity, Innovation, and Assurance Delivered—it is reinforced by ecosystem collaboration, targeted reskilling, and advanced Agentic AI for real-time execution and autonomous decision-making. The text positions TechM as an AI-first organization and partner to turn AI ambition into action.

nodes.title: CASE STUDY
nodes.summary:
CASE STUDY
AI Delivered Right in the real world
TechM and a Leading Indonesia Based Digital Telco Unite to Build Garuda, an LLM for Bahasa Indonesia and its Dialects

nodes.title: THE PARTNERSHIP
nodes.summary: Tech Mahindra signed an MoU at MWC 2024 to build 'Garuda', an LLM preserving Bahasa Indonesia and dialects, based on 'Project Indus'. Garuda will enable use cases like customer support, experience, and content creation across industries, with personalized experiences. It uses 16B original tokens and 1.2B parameters, with a beta release and improvement via RLHF and LIMA. The document also covers a case study of a UK network provider where AI-led automation streamlined field operations, achieving 38% auto-remediation and 30%/20% productivity gains. Another case study features a European CSP integrating AI/ML for predictive operations, targeting 80% automation and 50% call volume reduction by 2030.

nodes.title: THE SOLUTION
nodes.summary: The text presents two telecom case studies. First, a UK network provider facing efficiency pressures; TechM used intelligent automation, AI-led solutions, auto-healing, and AmazonQ to streamline field services, automate 38% of incident tickets, and improve greenfield and brownfield productivity by 30% and 20%, emphasizing responsible generative AI. Second, a European CSP pursuing 'Connect, Activate & Grow' struggled with legacy systems and manual processes; TechM integrated AI/ML for predictive operations across customer service, field operations, network management, and IT, shifting from reactive to predictive models to minimize downtime and optimize resources, putting the client on track for full operational autonomy by 2030 with 80% automation and 50% call volume reduction.

nodes.title: THE SOLUTION
nodes.summary: This document is Tech Mahindra's Integrated Annual Report for FY2024-25. It covers corporate overview including AI-led digital transformation case studies for telecom clients, the company's vision, values, global presence, service offerings, and industry verticals. It includes messages from the Chairman and MD & CEO discussing strategy, AI, trust, and progress on the three-year roadmap. The report details reporting frameworks, boundaries, and external assurance, and provides a table of contents. It also includes sections on strategy review, ESG, corporate governance, statutory reports, and financial statements. The text emphasizes AI Delivered Right, sustainability, and future-readiness.

nodes.title: LOOKING AHEAD
nodes.summary: The text covers the company's forward-looking statement for FY27, followed by a detailed key performance indicators section with financial metrics (revenue, EBITDA, net profit, EPS, dividend, free cash flow, net worth, cash equivalents) and non-financial metrics (women workforce, headcount, GHG emissions, CSR spending, active clients, renewable energy, water recycled, client buckets) from FY21 to FY25. It then presents the business model, outlining inputs and outputs across financial, service, intellectual, social/relationship, human, and natural capital. Finally, it includes strategy review elements: Rise tenets, ESG focus, innovation framework, guiding principles, competency development, alliance ecosystem, value creation process, and customer focus.

nodes.title: STRATEGY
nodes.summary: The STRATEGY section details Tech Mahindra's AI democratization strategy, including the 'AI Delivered Right' narrative, foundational pillars, FY27 vision 'Scale at Speed' with financial goals, a three-year roadmap, and strategic priorities in growth, operations, and organization. It covers stakeholder engagement (investors, customers, government, academic institutions, suppliers, employees, communities), the six-step materiality assessment process, FY25 materiality matrix with 20 topics, mapping to disclosures (GRI, SASB, etc.), and enterprise risk management including key risks (economic, cybersecurity, human capital, etc.) with mitigation strategies, ESG risk integration, and quantitative assessments. It also addresses AI risks and geopolitical/geo-economic fragmentation impacts and strategic shifts.

nodes.title: STRATEGY (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines Tech Mahindra's strategy to democratize AI across the organization, emphasizing its 'AI Delivered Right' narrative and foundational pillars: transformation, productivity, innovation, assurance, AI-ready talent, ecosystem collaboration, and recognitions. It presents the FY27 vision 'Scale at Speed' with financial goals, a three-year roadmap (turnaround, stabilization, reaping returns), and strategic priorities: growth (focus on key accounts, geographies, verticals, service lines), operations (Project Fortius for margin expansion), and organization (culture, talent, marketing, ESG). It includes FY25 progress, the CFO's message on financial performance and shareholder returns, and stakeholder engagement approach, including key stakeholders and the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee.

nodes.title: Academic Institutions
nodes.summary: This document outlines stakeholder engagement for FY25, covering academic institutions, suppliers, employees, customers, investors, partners, government, and local communities. It details collaboration for innovation and talent, supplier resilience and sustainability audits, and communication modes and concerns for each group. Employee initiatives address engagement, well-being, and diversity; customer feedback mechanisms and investor transparency are highlighted. Government compliance and community CSR programs are described. It also presents a double materiality assessment using impact and financial materiality, verified by DNV, aligned with GRI, SASB, and other standards, shaping strategy and value creation.

nodes.title: Strategy
nodes.summary: The text outlines TechM's strategy review process, including leadership change, business model, external factors (economic conditions, pandemics, natural disasters), and resource/customer expectations. It details a six-step materiality assessment process: identification of material topics using GRI, WEF, UN SDGs, SASB, and rating agencies; assessment of actual/potential impacts through impact and financial materiality; stakeholder engagement with internal/external parties; prioritization via severity rating; Board approval; and linkage to business strategy and performance through KPIs, Balanced Score Card, and incentive programs. It presents the FY25 materiality matrix with 20 topics (e.g., cybersecurity, climate change, human rights) and their management approaches, boundaries, risk/opportunity linkages, and disclosure mappings. It also covers scenario planning, ESG roadmap alignment, customer ESG assessments, and governance oversight.

nodes.title: Mapping to Disclosures
nodes.summary: This text outlines TechM's material topics and risk management. It maps various risks (financial, economic, revenue, business continuity, regulatory, supply chain, technology, market, competition) to disclosures like GRI standards and TechM Global. It details management approaches for talent and skill management, employee engagement, corporate citizenship, health and safety, energy management, diversity and inclusion, waste management, supply chain management, water stewardship, and biodiversity. Each topic includes boundary impact, risk/opportunity linkages, and mapping to GRI disclosures. The text also references page numbers for further reading on key performance indicators, integrated data governance, risk management, human capital, ESG roadmap, environmental practices, and supply chain management.

nodes.title: Mapping to Disclosures
nodes.summary: The text covers TechM's mapping of risks to disclosures: water stress and emerging regulation risks linked to GRI and TC-SI codes, biodiversity commitment, materiality impact on external stakeholders, and four key material issues for FY25: human rights (training, metrics), waste management (circular economy, metrics), energy management (renewable mix, GHG), and cybersecurity & data privacy (breach metrics). It then details enterprise risk management: FY25 environment, ERM agility and innovation, strategy, risk identification and reporting, risk culture, governance structure (Board, RMC, CRO, risk officers), process, communication, and a comprehensive table of key enterprise risks (economic slowdown, revenue, margin, impairment, cybersecurity, human capital, M&A integration, technology, delivery, legal, litigation, competition, geopolitical, compliance, immigration, IP, concentration, treasury/forex, branding, climate) with impacts and mitigation strategies. It integrates risks with strategy, covers ESG risk management framework, structure (three lines of control), audit, approach, risk categories, appetite and indicator scale, ESG risk analysis, application to strategy, and key ESG risks (physical, chronic, regulation, business continuity, technology, pollution, water stress, climate action failure, upstream/downstream value chain, reputation, market, legal, financial) with descriptions and mitigations. It includes quantitative assessment (sensitivity, stress testing, scenario analysis) for M&A, quality, water, climate, and emerging AI risks.

nodes.title: Impact
nodes.summary: The text addresses AI risks, including inherent biases, deepfakes, opacity, and delayed adoption leading to competitive disadvantage, plus job losses, misinformation, data privacy, dependency, inequality, regulatory lag, and transparency issues. Mitigation strategies involve investing in strategic technological competencies, continuous technology adoption via 'Scale at SpeedTM', upskilling programs, stakeholder engagement, and an ERM-integrated risk management strategy identifying AI risks in every business context. It also covers Geoeconomic Confrontation & Fragmentation (GEF), describing policy-induced reversal of global economic ties across trade, finance, and cooperation, with projected long-term global GDP losses of 0.2% to 12%.

nodes.title: Impact
nodes.summary: The text outlines geopolitical and geo-economic risks, including conflicts, energy and supply chain crises, inflation, and cyber threats. It details impacts on trade restrictions, commodity markets, tech export limits, and Net Zero goals, alongside labor mobility barriers. It describes strategic shifts to just-in-case models like nearshoring and stockpiling. The company TechM monitors macroeconomic headwinds affecting revenues and costs, evaluates opportunities, and notes its hybrid work environment expands talent pools and reduces recruitment limitations.

nodes.title: OPPORTUNITIES
nodes.summary: This section covers Tech Mahindra's opportunities in cloud, AI, and data analytics, alongside its integrated assurance statement. It details SASB-assured ESG metrics, TCFD-aligned disclosures, the FY22–FY26 ESG roadmap, and FY25 performance against targets. Environmental content includes climate action, net zero, GHG emissions (Scope 1, 2, 3), energy and water management, waste, and biodiversity. Social topics cover human capital, learning, diversity, pay equity, retention, wellness, health and safety, human rights, and CSR. Governance covers the ESG framework, board diversity, compliance, stakeholder relations, cybersecurity, data privacy, and memberships, with zero data breaches and reported highlights.

nodes.title: OPPORTUNITIES (intro)

nodes.title: CORE CONTENT – GOVERNANCE
nodes.summary: The text outlines governance disclosure requirements under IFRS S1-27. It covers the governance body or individuals responsible for overseeing sustainability-related risks and opportunities, including how responsibilities are reflected in terms of reference and policies, how skills and competencies are determined, how and how often they are informed, how they consider these risks in strategy, major transactions, and risk management (including tradeoffs), and how they oversee target setting and monitor progress, including links to remuneration. It also covers management’s role in governance processes, including delegation to specific positions or committees, oversight of that role, and the use of controls and procedures integrated with other internal functions.

nodes.title: CORE CONTENT – STRATEGY

It covers: (a) risks/opportunities affecting prospects and their time horizons; (b) definitions of short, medium, and long-term linked to strategic planning; (c) current and anticipated effects on business model and value chain, including concentration areas; (d) strategy and decision-making responses, progress against plans, and tradeoffs considered; (e) current and anticipated financial effects on financial position, performance, and cash flows, including significant adjustment risks and expected changes; and (f) resilience assessment of strategy and business model. Each disclosure is mapped to page locations in the report.

nodes.title: CORE CONTENT - RISK MANAGEMENT
nodes.summary: The text outlines IFRS S1 disclosure requirements for risk management. IFRS S1-44(a) requires entities to describe processes and policies for identifying, assessing, prioritising and monitoring sustainability-related risks, including: (i) inputs and parameters used (data sources, scope of operations); (ii) use of scenario analysis; (iii) assessment of nature, likelihood and magnitude of effects (qualitative factors, quantitative thresholds or other criteria); (iv) prioritisation relative to other risk types; (v) monitoring methods; and (vi) changes from the previous reporting period. IFRS S1-44(b) covers processes for sustainability-related opportunities, while IFRS S1-44(c) addresses how these risk and opportunity processes are integrated into and inform the entity's overall risk management process.

The Company has designed a comprehensive engagement program for new hires to help them integrate seamlessly. When it comes to shared services, automation continues to be a key focus area. Performance: People-centric
As part of the Culture change management project, your Company is making significant strides towards creating a simplified, transparent, innovative and performance-oriented workplace. With the launch of Insights 360, your Company has redefined performance management for its senior leaders. Through this, Leaders have discovered insights about their leadership styles, used feedback to improve performance and benefitted from focused coaching. The Company is also aligning its Job Family Framework (“JFF”) with market standards by updating job roles, titles and competencies. nodes.title: i) Financial assets

i) Financial assets
The Company applies the expected credit loss model for recognizing impairment loss on financial assets.
Expected credit loss is the difference between the contractual cash flows and the cash flows that the entity expects to receive discounted using effective interest rate.
Loss allowances for trade receivables are measured at an amount equal to lifetime expected credit losses. Lifetime expected credit losses are the expected credit losses that result from all possible default events over the expected life of a financial instrument. Lifetime expected credit loss is computed based on a provision matrix which takes into account historical credit loss experience adjusted for forward looking information. For other financial assets, expected credit loss is measured at the amount equal to twelve months expected credit loss unless there has been a significant increase in credit risk from initial recognition, in which case, those are measured at lifetime expected credit loss.

First, it covers the Provident Fund and National Pension Scheme (NPS), detailing that eligible employees and the Company make monthly contributions at a specified percentage of salary, charged to the Standalone statement of profit and loss on an accrual basis. Provident fund contributions are paid to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, with no further obligations for future provident fund benefits. Additionally, eligible employees and the Company contribute to the NPS, also a defined contribution plan. Second, it addresses Superannuation, another defined contribution scheme, where contributions are charged to the Standalone statement of profit and loss on an accrual basis, with no further obligations beyond annual contributions.

nodes.title: c. Compensated absences:
nodes.summary:
c. Compensated absences:
The Company provides for compensated absences and long term service awards subject to Company’s rules. The employees are entitled to accumulate leave subject to certain limits, for future encashment or availment. The liability is accrued based on the number of days of unavailed leave at each Balance Sheet date and the awards are accrued based on number of years of service of an employee. It is measured at the balance sheet date on the basis of an independent actuarial valuation using the Projected Unit Credit method.
Actuarial gains and losses are recognised in full in the Standalone statement of profit and loss in the period in which they occur.
The Company also offers a short term benefit in the form of encashment of unavailed accumulated compensated absences above certain limits as per respective policies and same is recognised as undiscounted liability at the balance sheet date.

Employee benefits are recognized when services are rendered. Dividend income is recognized when the right to receive is established; interest uses the effective interest rate method; rental income is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term, except when rentals increase with expected inflation. Taxation includes current and deferred tax, measured using enacted tax rates, recognized in profit or loss unless related to items in other comprehensive income or equity. Current tax covers Indian and overseas branches, with foreign tax credits generally available against Indian liability. Advance taxes and provisions are offset in the statement of financial position under specific conditions.

Instruments are categorized by fair value through P&L, fair value through OCI, derivative instruments in hedging relationship, and amortised cost, with totals for carrying value and fair value. A footnote clarifies that fair values of short-term instruments approximate carrying amounts. All amounts are in millions.

nodes.title: Assets:
nodes.summary: The text presents notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering financial instruments by category with carrying and fair values for 2025 and 2024, including assets like cash, receivables, investments, and liabilities such as payables and lease liabilities. It details fair value hierarchy levels (1, 2, 3) with tables for financial assets and liabilities, methods and assumptions for level 2 and level 3 valuations, and sensitivity of contractual obligations. Credit risk is discussed, including maximum exposure, trade receivables aging, expected credit loss allowance movement, and concentration risk. Market risk is briefly mentioned, focusing on foreign currency exchange risk.

nodes.title: a) Foreign currency exchange rate risk
nodes.summary: This text addresses foreign currency exchange rate risk, explaining that fluctuations can impact profit or loss, other comprehensive income, and equity when transactions involve multiple currencies or assets/liabilities are denominated in non-functional currencies. It notes risks primarily from USD, Euro, GBP, Australian Dollar, and Canadian Dollar fluctuations against the Company's functional currency. The Company uses derivative instruments to hedge foreign exchange risk per its risk management policy, evaluates exposure, and hedges part of the risks. It calculates sensitivity by aggregating net foreign exchange exposure and a simultaneous 1% shift in all currencies. The text provides carrying amounts of foreign currency denominated monetary assets and liabilities for March 31, 2025 and 2024, and shows the potential 1% strengthening impact on profit and loss for each currency.

nodes.title: b) Foreign Exchange Contracts
nodes.summary: The section on Foreign Exchange Contracts covers the Company's exposure to currency, credit, and liquidity risks, and its use of forward contracts to hedge forecasted transactions, including outstanding principal amounts, fair value gains/losses, and hedging reserve movements. It discusses liquidity risk management with tables of contractual maturities of financial liabilities as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, notes no borrowings secured by current assets, and confirms no willful default. It also provides a reconciliation of income tax expense to accounting profit, including tax effects and prior year adjustments. Additionally, the 'Particulars' subsection includes notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering contractual maturities as of March 31, 2024, secured borrowings and willful default confirmations, income tax reconciliation, deferred tax assets analysis, related parties and transactions, key managerial personnel remuneration, stock option exercises, entity-wise material transactions, Section 186 disclosures, investments in subsidiaries, ESOP schemes, earnings per share, regulatory information including financial ratios, investments/inter-corporate deposits, compliance statements on struck-off companies, crypto currency, layers of subsidiaries, and signatures of directors and auditors.

nodes.title: b) Foreign Exchange Contracts (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers foreign exchange contracts, including the Company's exposure to currency, credit, and liquidity risks, and its use of forward contracts to hedge forecasted transactions. It details outstanding principal amounts and fair value gains/losses for these contracts, and the movement in the hedging reserve. Liquidity risk management is discussed, with tables showing contractual maturities of financial liabilities as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. The text notes the Company has no borrowings secured by current assets and is not a willful defaulter. Finally, it provides a reconciliation of income tax expense to accounting profit, including tax effects and prior year adjustments.

nodes.title: Particulars
nodes.summary: The section 'Particulars' contains notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It covers contractual maturities of financial liabilities as of March 31, 2024, confirms no secured borrowings and no willful default, reconciles income tax expense to accounting profit, analyzes deferred tax assets and their movement, lists related parties and summarizes related party transactions and balances for 2025 and 2024 at arm's length. It also details key managerial personnel remuneration, stock option exercises, entity-wise material transactions, disclosures under Section 186 for loans and guarantees, investments in subsidiaries, ESOP schemes with grant, vesting and fair value assumptions, earnings per share calculations, additional regulatory information including financial ratios, details of investments/inter-corporate deposits to intermediaries, compliance statements on struck-off companies, crypto currency, and layers of subsidiaries, and includes signatures of directors and auditors.

It reconciles income tax expense to accounting profit, showing components like exempt income, disallowed expenses, prior-year taxes, and foreign branch taxes. Deferred tax assets and their movement by temporary difference are analyzed. It includes the auditor's opinion that the statements give a true and fair view in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013 and Ind AS. It covers the basis for opinion, emphasizing compliance with auditing standards and independence. An emphasis of matter discusses erstwhile Satyam claims. Key audit matters are revenue recognition on fixed price contracts and impairment of goodwill, detailing audit procedures. Other information, management's and auditor's responsibilities are outlined. Other matter notes reliance on other auditors for 72 subsidiaries. The report on other legal and regulatory requirements covers CARO, Section 143(3) matters, and Rule 11 compliance, including dividend, funds, and audit trail exceptions. Annexure A lists CARO qualifications, and Annexure B reports on internal financial controls.

nodes.title: OPINION

It outlines management's and board's responsibilities, the auditor's responsibility, definitions, inherent limitations, and reliance on other auditors. It also includes the consolidated balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, and cash flow statement, with detailed cash flow statements covering operating, investing, and financing activities, along with the consolidated statement of changes in equity for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, detailing equity share capital and other equity components, and notes describing each equity reserve, concluding with signatures and dates.

nodes.title: OPINION (intro)

It defines internal financial controls, notes inherent limitations including collusion and management override, and includes an other matter paragraph on reliance on other auditors and unaudited components deemed immaterial. The document also includes the consolidated balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, and cash flow statement, with signatures and dates.

It then covers changes in working capital including trade receivables, other assets, trade payables, unearned revenue, and other liabilities, followed by cash generated before taxes, income taxes paid, and net cash from operating activities.

nodes.title: B Cash Flow from Investing Activities

It lists various investing activities such as purchase and sale of property, plant, equipment, intangible assets, and investment property; purchase and redemption of mutual funds and other investments; payments for business acquisitions; rental income; fixed deposit/margin money placements and realizations; and interest income received. It provides a comparative table of amounts in millions for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, for each line item, culminating in net cash generated used in investing activities. The text also includes a reference to the consolidated statement of cash flow for the year ended March 31, 2025.

It also includes the consolidated statement of changes in equity for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, detailing equity share capital and other equity components such as reserves and surplus, share application money, capital reserves, securities premium, share option outstanding account, general reserve, statutory reserve, SEZ reinvestment reserve, capital redemption reserve, retained earnings, cash flow hedging reserve, equity instruments through OCI, and foreign currency translation reserve. nodes.title: 1. CORPORATE INFORMATION:
nodes.summary: Tech Mahindra Limited is described as a leading consulting-led integrated portfolio services provider for telecom equipment manufacturers, telecom service providers, IT infrastructure and BPO service providers, and enterprise solutions across BFSI, retail, logistics, manufacturing, energy and utilities, healthcare, and life sciences. It offers IT and IT-enabled services, application development and maintenance, consulting, enterprise business solutions, extended engineering solutions, and infrastructure management to diverse industries including insurance, banking, financial services, manufacturing, telecommunications, transportation, and engineering. The company is a public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office in Mumbai, and is listed on BSE and NSE. The Board approved the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, authorizing issue on April 24, 2025.

nodes.title: 2. MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICY INFORMATION:
nodes.summary: This section details material accounting policy information, including compliance with Ind AS and basis of consolidation, functional currency, measurement bases, fair value, and current/non-current classification. It covers cash flow statement preparation, business combinations, goodwill and intangible assets, and significant judgments and estimates for revenue recognition, income taxes, property plant and equipment, provisions, defined benefit plans, expected credit losses, and share-based compensation. Lease accounting as lessee and lessor, impairment of financial and non-financial assets, foreign currency translation, financial instruments (including derivatives and hedge accounting), derecognition, financial guarantee contracts, employee benefits, taxation, research and development, earnings per share, and recent pronouncements are also addressed. Finally, it presents various notes to the consolidated financial statements, including property plant and equipment, intangible assets, investments, trade receivables, loans, other financial assets, inventories, cash and cash equivalents, bank balances, equity, borrowings, provisions, income and expenses, consolidation particulars, non-controlling interests, commitments and contingencies, and other disclosures.

nodes.title: 2. MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICY INFORMATION: (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines material accounting policy information, covering the statement of compliance with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and the basis for preparing consolidated financial statements. It details the functional currency (INR for Indian entities, local currency for foreign subsidiaries), the use of historical cost and accrual basis except for certain financial instruments and defined benefit plans measured at fair value or amortized cost, and the definition and application of fair value. It also notes the classification of assets and liabilities as current/non-current based on a 12-month operating cycle and describes the preparation of the cash flow statement using the indirect method, including adjustments for non-cash items and the segregation of operating, investing, and financing cash flows, along with the treatment of cash equivalents.

nodes.title: Current/ non-current classification
nodes.summary: The text covers current/non-current classification criteria for assets and liabilities, including operating cycle definition, fair value measurement, and basis of consolidation for Tech Mahindra Limited (control definition, line-by-line consolidation, elimination of intra-group transactions, uniform accounting policies, non-controlling interests, changes in ownership without loss of control, and associate accounting using equity method). It also details business combinations using the purchase method, including cost measurement, identifiable assets/liabilities at fair value, non-controlling interest measurement, and contingent consideration. The text further references note 35 for consolidated entities and includes page numbering and report title.

nodes.title: Goodwill and intangible assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for goodwill and intangible assets, including goodwill impairment testing, measurement of separately acquired and business combination intangibles, and subsequent amortization. It details use of estimates and judgments in consolidated financial statements, with critical areas: revenue recognition using percentage of completion, performance obligations, transaction price allocation, and variable consideration; income and deferred taxes across India and USA; property, plant and equipment depreciation estimates; provisions and contingent liabilities; and business combinations under Ind AS 103 requiring fair valuation of net assets and contingent consideration.

nodes.title: Key Accounting Judgments: Income Taxes, PP&E, and Provisions
nodes.summary: This page from the Consolidated Financial Statements discusses significant judgments in three areas. First, revenue recognition uses an expected cost-plus margin approach to allocate transaction price. Second, income taxes and deferred taxes cover major jurisdictions (India and USA), judgments on tax positions, deferred tax on temporary differences, and realization dependent on future taxable profits, with policy reference Note 2.16. Third, property, plant and equipment address depreciation estimates of useful lives and residual values, reviewed annually and based on historical experience and future events, with policy reference Note 2.6. Finally, provisions and contingent liabilities explain recognition criteria, review at each balance sheet date, significant judgments for contingent liabilities, disclosure rules, and non-recognition of contingent assets, with policy reference Note 2.20.

nodes.title: Business combinations and intangible assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies under Ind AS 103 for business combinations, including fair valuation of identifiable net assets, contingent consideration, and intangible assets requiring significant estimates and independent valuations. It details annual goodwill impairment testing and factors considered, along with defined benefit plans and compensated absences using actuarial valuations with key assumptions. Expected credit losses on financial assets are based on assumptions about default risk and collection timing. Other estimates include share-based compensation. Finally, property, plant, and equipment and intangible assets are stated at cost less depreciation/amortization and impairment, with cost components and subsequent expenditure described.

nodes.title: Key Accounting Estimates and Impairment Policies
key_items: Defined benefit plans and compensated absences
Expected credit losses on financial assets
nodes.summary: This page discusses critical accounting estimates: impairment of goodwill, defined benefit plans and compensated absences, and expected credit losses on financial assets. Goodwill is tested annually or when indicators suggest impairment, using recoverable amount based on value-in-use or fair value less costs to sell, with key assumptions like growth rates, WACC, and operating margins. Defined benefit plans and compensated absences use actuarial valuation with assumptions on discount rates, salary increases, and mortality, reviewed at each reporting date. Expected credit losses rely on assumptions about default risk and collection timing, using historical data, creditworthiness, market conditions, and forward-looking estimates.

nodes.title: Other estimates
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: share-based compensation expense based on estimated vesting equity instruments; property, plant & equipment and intangible assets measured at cost less depreciation/amortisation and impairment, including cost components, capital work in progress, depreciation methods and useful lives, amortisation of intangibles, derecognition, and reclassification to investment property; investment property measured at cost less depreciation and impairment, depreciation methods and useful lives, and derecognition; and lease identification criteria.

nodes.title: Group as a lessee
nodes.summary: The text details the Group's accounting as a lessee, covering right-of-use asset recognition, measurement, depreciation, impairment, and lease liability measurement including discount rates and remeasurement. It also addresses lessor accounting, including lease classification, income recognition for operating and finance leases, sub-leases, and allocation of lease and non-lease components. Additionally, it outlines impairment of financial assets using the expected credit loss model and impairment of non-financial assets.

nodes.title: Lease Accounting and Financial Asset Impairment Policies
nodes.summary: The page outlines the Group's accounting policies for leases and impairment of financial assets. As lessor, it classifies leases as operating or finance, recognizes income accordingly, and addresses intermediate lessor treatment and lease/non-lease components. As lessee, it adjusts right-of-use assets for lease liability remeasurements and exempts short-term and low-value leases. For impairment, the Group applies the expected credit loss model, measuring loss allowances for trade receivables at lifetime expected credit losses using a provision matrix, and for other financial assets at twelve-month expected credit losses unless credit risk significantly increased.

nodes.title: ii) Non-financial assets
nodes.summary: This text outlines the accounting policy for non-financial assets, specifically property, plant, and equipment and intangible assets with finite life. It details that these assets are evaluated for recoverability whenever there is an indication of potential impairment. The recoverable amount, defined as the higher of fair value less cost to sell and value-in-use, is determined on an individual asset basis unless the asset does not generate largely independent cash flows, in which case it is determined for the Cash Generating Unit (CGU) to which the asset belongs. If the recoverable amount is less than the carrying amount, the carrying amount is reduced to the recoverable amount, and an impairment loss is recognized in the Consolidated statement of profit and loss. The text also includes a reference to the financial statements notes for the year ended March 31, 2025.

nodes.title: iii) Goodwill
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for goodwill impairment testing, revenue recognition under Ind AS 115 (including five-step approach, contract types, contract assets/liabilities, principal vs. agent, discounts, and contract modifications), foreign currency transactions and operations translation, and financial instruments (initial and subsequent measurement, amortised cost, fair value, and financial liabilities).

nodes.title: Notes on Foreign Operations and Financial Instruments Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: Covers translation of foreign operations: assets/liabilities at closing rates, income/expenses at average rates, exchange differences in OCI and equity, and transfer to profit on subsidiary disposal. Details financial instrument recognition at fair value (trade receivables at transaction price) and treatment of transaction costs. Describes non-derivative instruments: cash equivalents (highly liquid, ≤3 months), financial assets at amortised cost (held to collect contractual cash flows, effective interest method less impairment), and financial assets at fair value (FVTPL unless irrevocable OCI election for non-trading equity instruments; FVTPL remeasurement gains/losses in profit or loss). Also covers financial liabilities at amortised cost or FVTPL, with amortised cost approximating fair value due to short maturities.

nodes.title: Financial liabilities
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 for the year ended March 31, 2025. It covers foreign operations translation: assets/liabilities at closing rates, income/expenses at average rates, exchange differences in other comprehensive income, and transfer to profit/loss on disposal. Financial instruments are recognized when the Group becomes a party, initially at fair value (except trade receivables at transaction price), with transaction costs added/deducted except for FVTPL items. Non-derivative instruments include cash equivalents (highly liquid, ≤3 months), financial assets at amortized cost (effective interest method, impairment), and financial assets at fair value (FVTPL or irrevocable OCI election for non-trading equity). Financial liabilities are at amortized cost or FVTPL, with gains/losses in profit or loss.

nodes.title: ii) Derivative financial instruments and hedge accounting
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Group's use of derivative financial instruments for hedging foreign currency risks, specifically cash flow hedges using forward contracts under Ind AS 109. It details the risk management policy, initial and subsequent measurement at fair value, recognition of effective and ineffective hedge portions in other comprehensive income and profit or loss, reclassification of accumulated gains/losses, treatment of derivatives not qualifying for hedge accounting, and conditions for discontinuing hedge accounting.

nodes.title: Derecognition of financial instruments
nodes.summary:
Derecognition of financial instruments
The Group derecognises a financial asset when the contractual rights to the cash flows from the asset expire, or when it transfers the financial asset and substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership of the asset to another party. The cost associated

nodes.title: iv) Financial Guarantee contracts

nodes.title: 45.1 Accounting for sales commission

Pending legal disputes between Tech Mahindra Ltd and Venture Global LLC, a contingency provision of ₹529 million was made for FY 2005-2006 to FY 2011-2012. Following a High Court order to maintain status quo, the provision was not reversed based on legal opinion. Subsequent sales commission is disclosed as a contingent liability of ₹3,893 million as of March 31, 2025, compared to ₹3,535 million as of March 31, 2024.

nodes.title: Allocation of goodwill to cash-generating units
nodes.summary: The text details goodwill impairment testing: annual or triggered testing, allocation to cash-generating units (CGUs) based on business units, and testing at the lowest level monitored. Recoverable amount is the higher of value-in-use and fair value less costs to sell, with value-in-use used when fair value is unreliable. Value-in-use considers cash flow projections from approved budgets. Key assumptions include terminal growth rates, weighted average cost of capital, and operating margins. Cash flows cover five years with 2%-4% growth thereafter, and margins reflect past experience and revenue volume. Pre-tax discount rates range from 13.2%-32.68% (prior year: 14%-30%). Impairment losses are allocated first to goodwill, then pro-rata to other assets.

nodes.title: 49.1.Impairment of Goodwill

It provides a table of impairment amounts and recoverable amounts for CGUs including Target Topco Group and CTC Group, noting these are subsumed into new CGUs. It explains that value-in-use calculations use entity-specific future cash flow estimates based on approved business plans and consider economic risks, volume forecasts, margins, and discount rates. Key assumptions are listed: discount rates, terminal growth rates, and budgeted EBITDA growth rates. Cash flow projections cover five years plus terminal growth, with sensitivity analysis on discount rates and growth rates.
